### Changed

- The `programming` skill's language gate now routes rendered web work (`.html`, `.css`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, `.astro`, or any task that ships a UI) to the `frontend` skill before the first line of UI code. It tells the agent to take the look from the frontend skill's references when there is no design direction (no named brand, reference, `DESIGN.md`, or existing styled UI to match), and to finish only after `visual-qa` passes on the rendered surface. ([#14604](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14604), fixes [#14602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14602))

### Fixed

- Memory sync: a sign-out now retires the trust pin of the account it signs out of, so `omo account show --account <id>` no longer answers `joined` once that sign-in's keys are gone. Plain `omo account forget` (the desktop's sign-out of a CLI-item session) used to retire nothing. It now reads the stored sign-in first to find its account. A stored sign-in that cannot be read is still deleted and its pin is left; one warning line is printed only after the delete succeeds. A forget that fails on a locked store reports only that error (#12308, #12384). ([#13642](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13642)) ([#14533](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14533))
- Memory sync: some sign-ins earned their pin before `omo sync` recorded their account. On a refused refresh, plain `forget`, `forget --device` and `adopt --replace`, omo now asks the service for that account, as `omo logout` already did, and retires the pin when the service names it. It asks only while a live pin exists and the access token has not expired; on a refused refresh, the token may still be valid in the 30 s before expiry, when the refresh runs. An expired token is never sent. A pin whose account stays unknown is kept, and omo prints one line naming `omo account retire-sync --account <id>` to clear it, because `omo account show` keeps answering `joined` for it (#12383, #13662). ([#13642](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13642)) ([#14533](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14533))

### Added

- `omo sync status` (and `--json`) shows this device's memory sync state: the signed-in account, whether this device has joined and whether its sync switch is on, the account's devices with their sync membership and last-seen time, pending join requests, and whether an engine is running on this machine. It writes no sync state, prints no key material, and each section reports its own failure instead of failing the command. ([#14437](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14437), fixes [#14435](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14435)) ([#14533](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14533))

### Fixed

- The `/remote` close in the TUI follows `thread_close`'s close contract (#14234). A close refused because the thread has messages it has not read names `/remote close <session> --force` and lists those messages, or says the ids are unavailable on that device's engine. The picker then offers "Close anyway". A forced close lists the messages it dropped. The refusal's `details.reason` is the engine's own reason (`turn_active` or `work_pending`). ([#14246](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14246), fixes [#14245](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14245)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))
- Thread tools: a command for a thread whose session parked on another device after it was listed no longer fails `unsupported` with advice to update omo on that device. The device service answers such a command `route_unlisted` (its host no longer lists that session, so nothing was sent to it). `thread_close` now answers `closed: false, reason: "not_live"`, and the other thread tools answer `not_resumable`, as for a session that ended there. A create, or a reopen's session-file lookup, refused that way is `host_unavailable`, with a retry. ([#14237](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14237), fixes [#14233](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14233)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))
- The cold-wake session host unit (and every other unit or plist the cold-wake install writes) is now written 0644 under any umask. Under umask 077 it was written 0600, because a file's creation mode is masked by the umask; the mode is now set explicitly before the file is moved into place. ([#14249](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14249), fixes [#14247](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14247)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))
- A cold-wake unit or plist an earlier build already left 0600 is set back to 0644 the next time the install (or a refresh to a newer runtime) finds its content unchanged, with no reload or restart. A file this user cannot change the mode of (another owner's, or on a read-only filesystem) is left as it is and the install still succeeds. ([#14249](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14249)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))

### Changed

- **`thread_close` no longer drops messages a thread has not read unless you ask it to.** Before, it always interrupted the session and silently dropped any messages queued behind its run. Now:
  - A busy thread with unread messages is refused `turn_active`. The refusal names those messages (`pending_deliveries`) and gives the `force` option.
  - `thread_close({ thread, force: true })` closes it anyway.
  - Every close result carries `dropped_deliveries`, the messages it handed back unread (an empty list when there were none).
  - An idle thread still closes without `force`, even when an interrupted run left messages stranded (#14169); those are listed too.
  - On a device whose engine cannot name its queued messages (older than code-yeongyu/senpi#7006), a default close never interrupts. It says the message ids are unavailable there, and `force: true` still closes it.
  - `omo remote close` takes `--force` and reports the dropped messages as well. ([#14242](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14242), fixes [#14234](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14234)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))

### Added

- The desktop can ask OmO which model each category and agent runs. A new read-only extension request, `omo.modelRouting.resolve`, answers the model every category (under its canonical name) and every task agent would spawn on, using the same resolvers a `task` call uses against the session's project config, model registry and sign-ins, and says whethe

### Changed

- Hephaestus on GPT-6.2 models sends one prompt instead of two: the GPT-6.2 core stands alone there, so the Hephaestus role is no longer appended after it. Other models keep the role, and switching models in a session drops or restores it. On a real request the system prompt goes from 9,211 to 4,300 tokens (`o200k_base`). The refusal-is-final rule is now stated once inside the model-core frame for every agent that carries it instead of at the end of the role, so it survives without the role and is never doubled by a model core that states it. ([#14219](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14219), part of [#14186](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14186)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- **No behaviour change: tests now pin which ended sessions a fuzzy handoff compares.** A fuzzy handoff still compares only the ended sessions that could change its answer. Tests now prove the cut-off, and that a session left out never appears in the list an ambiguous handoff asks you to pick from. ([#13190](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13190), follows #13141) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Thread tools in one process share a single endpoint enumeration per agent dir, instead of one per session, so a session that a delivery just started reuses a listing taken within the last 5 s. ([#13236](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13236), part of [#12989](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12989)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **Every recovery hint in the thread tools now gives the eval-cell form beside the tool name (`thread_list (tool.thread_list() in an eval cell)`), the convention the thread tool descriptions already follow.** A model that follows a hint no longer hits the "run it in an eval cell" redirect first. ([#13240](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13240)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- A thread tool call on an account with other devices reads the account's session list once instead of up to three times: overlapping reads share one listing round, and a round that ended under 2 s ago answers the next read (a create, open or session command lists again). The account list waits on every device, 0.5-2 s on a loaded fleet. ([#13453](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13453)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- `thread_list` rows carry a `state` (`running`, `idle`, `inactive` or `archived`) and the thread's `model` when known, instead of a per-thread live/alive flag; whether a device is reachable is on `devices` only. Archived threads are hidden unless a `state` filter asks for them (`omo thread list --state`), and a thread closed on this device stays listed as inactive instead of disappearing. `status` remains for now, derived from the state. ([#13469](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13469), fixes [#13403](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13403)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **`omo remote` takes a device by the name its table prints.** The session verbs (`open`, `send`, `model`, `interrupt`, `close`) accept a device's id, its name (compared as thread names are) or a unique id prefix, through the same resolver `thread_create` uses, and their output names the device by its id. A name two online devices share is refused with `ambiguous_target`, listing each candidate; a name only an offline device has is `device_offline`; a device nothing matches is `not_found`. ([#13499](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13499), [#13432](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13432)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- The thread control port's `setThinkingLevel`

**On Windows, a busy sign-in lock now names the process holding it.** `omo login`, `whoami` and `logout` used to report the holder as exited or unreadable whenever it was still running, so the message gave no pid and no fix. They now name its pid and image (read with `tasklist`), the lock path, and `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` as the way to end it. ([#14118](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14118), refs #14001)

### Changed

- GPT lanes (`ultrabrain`, `deep-high`, `deep-low`, `unspecified-low`), the plan reviewer and both Obsessive profiles lead with GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol stay right behind at the same effort, so an engine or provider without 6.2 (including GitHub Copilot) keeps the models it ran before. GPT-6.2 ids get the low..max effort ladder, and `none` and `minimal` are sent as `low`. (#14126) ([#14149](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14149))
- OmO now runs on senpi 2026.11.18 (from 2026.11.15-4), the release that carries the GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol catalog rows and the `gpt-6.2` prompt preset. (#14126) ([#14149](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14149))
- **Thread tool rows in the TUI now read like a status line instead of a JSON dump.** Each `thread_*` tool shows one call line (the verb, the target thread's name or short id, and the message's first line) and one outcome line with a few short details: `-> planner  follow-up delivered (turn 306)`, `planner: 12 messages (latest: ...)`, `3 threads in this workspace` with the first few threads, `created scratch`. Delivery ids, message sequence numbers and full uuids stay out of the collapsed row; a failure shows its code, message and next step; the expanded view (ctrl+o) adds the full result. What the model receives is unchanged. ([#12997](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12997)) ([#14141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14141))

### Fixed

- A `thread_send` to a busy thread on another device that was queued there as a follow-up now answers `queued` with its `delivery_id` and `effective_mode`. It used to answer `idempotency_uncertain` ("accepted the message but did not report where it waits") even though the message was delivered and answered. The receiving engine's `queued` admission is its receipt, and its pending-message count does not include admitted deliveries. ([#14013](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14013), fixes [#14012](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14012)) ([#14141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14141))
- A reply to a peer on another device no longer answers `not_found` when the delivery that brought the peer's message carries no device attestation (an `rpc:local/<id>` or bare delivery id). If this device holds no session by that id or stated name, the reply is looked up account-wide. It is delivered only to the session the sender's durable id names; another match is `reply_target_mismatch`, and an id that more than one device lists is `ambiguous_target` with nothing sent. ([#14052](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14052)) ([#14141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14141))
- `thread_create` with a `prompt` gives the new thread that prompt as its own first user message, with the creator's authority, instead of a relayed peer message under the gateway header. A later `thread_send` from any session, the creator included, keeps the relay header. ([#14058](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14058)) ([#14141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14141))
- `omo -p` exits again after the run calls a thread tool. The device-service connection a thread tool opened is now closed when the session shuts down, so it no longer keeps a finished print-mode run alive. ([#14062](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14062)) ([#14141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14141))
- T

### Fixed

- `omo remote devices` shows this device offline while its device service is not connected, and `omo remote sessions --device` naming a device the account does not have reports it instead of listing nothing. ([#13916](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13916))
- Memory sync's own test suite no longer fails a later, unrelated test when one test times out while a sync cycle is still running: device teardown in the tests now stops the engine and waits for that cycle before removing its files, and the push-bounded test waits on the cycle instead of a fixed 30 s budget. ([#13887](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13887), fixes [#13680](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13680))
- The first memory sync cycle after signing in no longer fails with "the device's sign-in token could not be read or refreshed" when the system keychain briefly reads nothing. That one empty read is now checked again before sync treats the sign-in as gone; signing out still stops sync at once. ([#13879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13879), fixes [#13739](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13739))
- Regenerating the computer-use prelude (`bun run generate` in `senpi-desktop-prelude`) now runs its generated method tables through `bun fmt`, so `prelude.js`, its `index.ts` allowlist and the desktop protocol tier tables stay formatter-clean instead of reverting to unformatted output at every release regeneration. The published prelude JavaScript is the formatted copy again. ([#13855](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13855))

### Changed

- A memory sync capture that receives files from other devices no longer scans every known file once per received file, so a large memory catching up on many incoming files stays fast. ([#13862](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13862))
